main_issue: Whether and how strong-smelling cooking (D's salted fish) can continue in the shared flat, e.g. via containment measures, timing after 7pm or Saturdays, and warning B.

A-B.evidence: Both opposed the smell at start (T2-3). A's containment plan (T13) was met with B's 'still gets into the living room' (T14). A backed B (T17). B accepted a warn-and-close-door arrangement (T18, T21), and A endorsed the final arrangement (T26).

A-C.evidence: C complained about laundry smell (T5) and accepted A's closed yard door (T15). A's containment plan addressed C's concern, and C raised no further objection.

A-D.evidence: D resisted: 'it's the only kitchen' (T8, T12). D then agreed 'I can do that' (T16) and 'After 7pm is fine' (T22). A concluded 'that's what we'll do' (T26).

B-C.evidence: B and C jointly argued that the laundry smell persists regardless of time (T10-11). C accepted the closed yard door (T15), and B's remaining concern (T14, T18) was resolved separately.

B-D.evidence: D resisted the restrictions (T8, T12). B asked to be told before cooking; D replied 'I can tell you' (T20), and B answered 'That works' (T21).

C-D.evidence: C objected to the laundry smell (T5, T11). D said 'I can do that' to closing the yard door (T16), and C had said that this works for them (T15).
